finding: Selected packed planning/execution created a two-number array per visited row. Gather/concat used separate range access and did not reject payload extents beyond the visible data view.
fix: Share scalar packed-byte start/length access between gather/concat and selected planning/execution, removing per-row range tuples.
Validate safe nonnegative row/start/length and payload boundaries before gather output admission, including visible subarray bounds.
Read fixedLength once while measuring a range, preserving existing exact traversal-count tests.

validation.conformance: Two pre-identity full attempts and an isolated page-count query exceeded the unchanged timeout. Generic physical identity-projection follow-up now passes all 520 required cases (one inactive guard skipped), with a measured ~20% local query improvement. See physical-identity-projection-2026-11-14.json.

negativeControl.result: Baseline compactGatherPlan accepts an out-of-bounds packed range; current helper rejects with LAKEQL_VALIDATION_ERROR before allocation.

benchmark.binaryCases: All four binary cases improve in both runs.
benchmark.scope: Alternating local plan+execute; prior selected-packed module uses current dependencies. Not a complete historical build or a cloud measurement. Peak admitted output is unchanged; all owners release to zero.

rejectedAlternative.decision: Do not replace all native subarray/set copies with scalar loops. Tiny ranges favor loops, but large ranges strongly favor native copying. No new production threshold or configuration added.

regressionEvidence: Initial full suite: 3896 passed, one traversal-count failure from reading fixedLength twice. Reused the measured length for fixed-width start validation; existing traversal assertions then pass unchanged.
Malformed range tests cover visible subarrays, negative/fractional/nonfinite fixed lengths and row offsets; null hidden ranges remain unread and empty end-of-payload values remain valid.
boundaries: Native copy/encoding subarray views still need explicit scratch accounting; this change removes range tuples, not every temporary allocation.
Packed output descriptors and planner containers remain separate accounting gaps.
The release-gate refresh on beebd97 predates this runtime change; full acceptance remains open.
